assessment.nobel_worthiness: Correcting spherical aberration in the electron microscope removed a limit that had stood since Scherzer's 1936 theorem and opened routine sub-angstrom imaging and spectroscopy of atoms, interfaces and defects across physics, materials science and chemistry. This is a tool that opens a door to phenomena that could not be seen before, and it is an invention with an unambiguous, verifiable result.
assessment.attribution: Rose supplied the theoretical corrector designs, Haider led construction of the first working hexapole corrector for the TEM, and Urban drove the experimental realization and application together with Haider. This is a natural and compact three-person configuration. Others such as Krivanek (STEM correction) are not in the supplied credit, so the allocation between TEM and STEM correction would need careful historical review.
assessment.maturity: Demonstrated in 1997-1998 and now installed in laboratories worldwide, with decades of independent confirmation and heavy use. Recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: The supplied credit omits the parallel STEM-corrector line (Krivanek and collaborators), so it is unclear whether a fair prize can be built from these three names alone.
Whether the committee regards this as physics rather than instrumentation for materials science, and my own field proximity means colleagues should check my judgement.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Theoretical prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle followed by the experimental observation of correlated insulating and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene (2018) created the field of moire quantum materials. The original experiment was clear, striking and reproduced widely, and it gave a tunable platform for correlated physics.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the key 2011 prediction of the magic angle, and Jarillo-Herrero's group did the original 2018 experiments (with Yuan Cao as lead author, who is not in the supplied credit). The three supplied names form a coherent theory-plus-experiment configuration. Credit overlaps with the early theory and experimental work of others, notably Dean, Kim and Young's graphene moire work, which the supplied list does not include.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by many independent groups with a stable interpretation of the correlated phases, although the nature of the superconductivity is still debated.
uncertainties: The mechanism of superconductivity in magic-angle graphene remains unsettled.
Credit for the earlier moire graphene experiments and for the lead student or postdoc authors is outside the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2006-2008 discovery of superconductivity in LaFeAsO(1-x)F(x) opened the second family of high-temperature superconductors, with Tc above 50 K soon reached. It is a clear original materials discovery, experimentally verified, and it stimulated a large field on unconventional pairing.
assessment.attribution: Kamihara and Hosono reported the first iron-pnictide superconductor and the lead publication is unambiguous. Earlier work by Hosono's group on LaFePO is part of the same story. The two-person configuration is simple and fits the discovery-oriented criterion.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced immediately worldwide and the family has been studied for about eighteen years. The pairing mechanism is not settled, but the discovery itself is secure.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism remains debated, and the committee may prefer to wait for greater theoretical clarity.
The 2008 paper appeared in a chemistry journal, so questions of priority and the earlier LaFePO observation should be checked.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators are one of the major conceptual and experimental developments in condensed matter physics of this century, with a quantized edge conductance in HgTe quantum wells and spin-momentum-locked surface states in Bi-Sb and Bi2Se3 seen directly by photoemission.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele proposed the quantum spin Hall state, Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang predicted it in HgTe, Molenkamp's group observed it in 2007, and Hasan's group observed 3D topological insulators. Selecting three of these names necessarily leaves out deserving contributors, and a prize would sit uneasily with the 2016 topological-phase prize. The theory contributions of Mele and the HgTe prediction by Zhang and colleagues are difficult to separate fairly, and I choose experimental observation plus the principal theorist.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature, with extensive independent confirmation and technological interest, although practical applications are limited.
uncertainties: Fair allocation between Kane, Mele, the HgTe theorists and the experimentalists is unresolved and the supplied credit omits Zhang, Bernevig and Hughes.
The relation to the 2016 prize on topological phase transitions may weigh against timing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The IceCube observation of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos in 2013, followed by evidence of the blazar TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane, opened neutrino astronomy at TeV-PeV energies. It is a new window on the universe built from an instrument that turned a cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice into a detector.
assessment.attribution: Halzen was the intellectual leader of IceCube and its predecessor AMANDA, with Karle and Spiering as key experimental leaders. The large collaboration makes the allocation of credit among individuals difficult, and the fair configuration is not obvious.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is firmly established and independently supported by ANTARES-type detectors, while source identification is still partial. Recognition would be reasonable but arguably early for the source-identification part.
uncertainties: Source associations such as TXS 0506+056 and NGC 1068 are still few and the picture of cosmic-ray acceleration is incomplete.
Credit beyond the three named people, including the earlier DUMAND, Baikal and AMANDA pioneers, is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Katori's magic-wavelength optical lattice proposal and its experimental realization, developed by Ye into clocks with fractional uncertainty around 1e-18, transformed precision measurement. The work gives a tool that opens a door to tests of relativity, searches for varying constants and relativistic geodesy.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the optical lattice clock concept (2001-2003) and Ye's group advanced it to the highest accuracy. The two-person credit is clean, though other contributors such as the single-ion clock groups and frequency-comb developers have been recognized elsewhere.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups reproduce the performance and the work is moving toward a redefinition of the second. This is mature, though the largest applied consequences are still to come.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2005 Nobel Prize for frequency combs (Hall and Hansch) and with the ion-clock prize of 2012 may reduce the perceived novelty.
Whether the original proposal or the later accuracy record is considered the decisive step.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 1995 observation of large room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions was an original experiment that made spintronic readout and MRAM practical. Its impact on hard-disk heads and non-volatile memory is large and it complements the 2007 GMR prize.
assessment.attribution: Moodera's group and Miyazaki's group independently reported room-temperature TMR in 1995, which makes these two a natural pair. Parkin's later giant TMR in MgO junctions, together with the Yuasa and Djayaprawira work, is also part of the story and the credit among them is a difficult allocation. Julliere's 1975 low-temperature observation is a historical precursor that the committee would need to weigh.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, with decades of independent confirmation and commercial use.
uncertainties: Choosing between Moodera and Miyazaki on the one hand and Parkin and the MgO group on the other, and the role of Julliere's precursor, is unresolved.
The overlap with the 2007 GMR prize may make the committee reluctant.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2012 observation of the Higgs boson by ATLAS and CMS completed the experimental confirmation of the Standard Model mechanism for mass and is a landmark, experimentally verified discovery of the original particle.
assessment.attribution: The discovery was made by two collaborations of thousands of people, and the committee is bound by the statutes to name at most three persons. Gianotti, Della Negra and Virdee were respectively spokesperson and project leaders with Jenni, so attribution to individuals is arbitrary, and I am not comfortable that these particular names identify who did the original work. The theoretical prize of 2013 has already recognized the prediction.
assessment.maturity: The discovery is firmly confirmed and the properties of the boson have been measured for over a decade. Timing is no obstacle, though the 2013 prize reduces the urgency.
uncertainties: No fair three-person configuration exists for a collaboration discovery, and any choice would be disputed.
The committee has historically been reluctant to honour large-collaboration leadership roles as the original experimental contribution.
